evidence.note: Establishes foundations-first sequencing: inspect workspace and match the /dev_tests/helpers.py contract, then read visible tests to pin request/response shapes before building — a dependency-respecting opening.

Surveys the whole surface (formulas, arrays, propagation, CSV/XLSX, collab, formats, pivots, locale, validation, iterative calc) and sequences service entrypoint + dependency bootstrap + foreground server first, before the app — foundations before features.

Builds the core as one monolithic module then plans to run the visible suite 'in slices' to catch contract/evaluator defects — a rough done-check gate, but not milestone-gated incremental construction.

Phase progression with rough completion criteria: 'base API and formula corpus passing → moving to stateful behavior (cycles, spill, fill, sort/filter, import/export)' then 'all visible tests passing → hardening pass.' Later features deferred until earlier phases pass.

Final phase adds an explicit restart/persistence done-check ('manual restart check for persisted state') and full-suite rerun — verification gates exist per phase but were never enumerated as an upfront milestone map with per-item done criteria.

reasoning: The agent follows a sensible, dependency-aware order — contract recon → bootable server/health/persistence → core cell model+engine → stateful behaviors → hardening → restart check — with rough per-phase done-checks (suite slices, all-visible-passing, restart persistence), which clearly exceeds the flat undifferentiated list of anchor 3 and satisfies anchor 5's 'foundations first with rough milestones.' It falls short of anchor 8 because the decomposition is a rolling post-hoc narrative rather than an explicit milestone hierarchy where each piece names its confirmation up front, the build was one monolithic module rather than incrementally gated, and cross-cutting invariants (e.g. WebSocket cells == REST patch shape) were never called out as shared milestones. That places it between 5 and 8, at 6.
